function: above_phy: the TDQN agent learns UAV 3D movement and GT scheduling; the RIS phase shift is calculated from the UAV position, not learned (pp. 3, 7).
notes: Excluded as above_phy. The learned action is a(t) = {l_t, h_t, c_u,n,t}: p. 7 "the movements of the UAV in the horizontal direction (forward, backward, left, right, and hover) and in the vertical direction (up, down, and hover)" and "The cu,n,t represents the scheduling decision of the GT n." The RIS phase shift is not in the action: p. 3 "the planned UAV positions for each time slot are used to calculate the phase shift of the RIS to maximize the channel gain"; p. 6 says only that "aligning the UAV-RIS-GT link maximizes the signal gain received between the UAV and the GT", and Algorithm 2 (p. 9) lists the step "Design the RIS’s phase shift" apart from the action a(t), with no learned model described for it. So no physical-layer decision is learned jointly with the trajectory and scheduling ones. Not no_learning, since the DRL is the main method and acts on UAV trajectory and scheduling, which rule 4 names. The paper links its code on p. 9 (github.com/NetworkCommunication/TDQN).
